answer: When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 5 times its size, so a group of 93 keys loses far more than 93 single identities would. The sonnet graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the raven audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the nebula checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
